source_text: Primo, supercilio stuporem suum aedificant Marcionitae, quod nouum deum proferant, quasi nos ueteris dei pudeat. inflantur et pueri nouis calceis, sed a uetere paedagogo calceati mox uanam gloriam uapulabunt. nouum igitur audiens deum, in uetere mundo et in uetere aeuo et sub uetere deo ignotum inauditum, quem, tantis retro saeculis neminem et ipsa ignorantia antiquum, quidam Iesus Christus, et ille in ueteribus nominibus nouus, reuelauerit, nec alius antehac. gratias ago huic gloriae eorum, maximo adiutorio eius hinc iam haeresim probaturus, nouae scilicet diuinitatis professionem. haec erit nouitas, quae etiam ethnicis deos peperit nouo, semper ac nouo titulo consecrationis cuiusque. quis deus nouus nisi falsus? ne Saturnum quidem tanta hodie antiquitas deum probabit, quia et illum nouitas aliquando produxerit.. cum primum consecrauit. atenim uiua et germana diuinitas nec de nouitate nec de uetustate, sed de sua ueritate cense-!i tur. non habet tempus aeternitas. omne enim tempus ipsa, est. quod facit, pati non potest. caret aetate quod non licet\' nasci. deus si est uetus, non erit, si est nouus, non fuit., nouitas initium testificatur, uetustas finem comminatur. deus autem tam alienus ab initio et fine est quam a tempore, arbitro et metatore initii et finis.I
pass_a_gloss: First, Marcionites build their amazement on the fact that they bring forth a new God, as if we are ashamed of the old God. Children also puff themselves up with new shoes, but soon, shod by an old teacher, they will suffer the penalty of empty glory. Therefore, hearing of a new God, unknown and unheard of in the old world and in the old age and under the old God, whom no one and ignorance itself knew as ancient, a certain Jesus Christ, and he in old names new, revealed, and no other before, I give thanks to this glory of theirs, the greatest help to me, who will now prove their heresy, namely the profession of a new divinity. This will be the novelty that even produced new gods for the pagans with a new and always new title of consecration of each. What new God is there except a false one? Not even great antiquity will prove Saturn to be a God today, because novelty once brought him forth, when he was first consecrated. For living and genuine divinity is reckoned not from novelty or antiquity, but from its own truth. Eternity does not have time. For all time is itself. What it does, it cannot suffer. It lacks age because it is not allowed to be born. If God is old, he will not be; if he is new, he was not. Novelty testifies to a beginning, antiquity threatens an end. But God is as alien to beginning and end as to time, the arbiter and measurer of beginning and end.

pass_b_english: The Marcionites open their case with a flourish: they parade a 'new God' as if we should be embarrassed by the old one. Children puff themselves up over new shoes, too, but an old schoolmaster soon makes them pay for their empty pride. So they announce a new God—unknown, unheard of in the old world, the old age, under the old God—whom no one knew, not even ignorance itself, as ancient, until a certain Jesus Christ revealed him. And he did it in old names, yet made them new. No one else had done it before. I thank them for this boast; it is the greatest help I could ask for in proving their heresy—the claim of a new divinity. That is the kind of novelty that even spawned new gods for the pagans, each consecrated with a brand-new, ever-new title. What is a new god but a false one? Not even Saturn’s vast antiquity makes him a god today, because novelty once produced him, back when he was first consecrated. Living, genuine divinity is measured not by novelty or antiquity, but by its own truth. Eternity has no time; it is all time. What it does, it cannot undergo. It has no age, because it cannot be born. If God is old, he will cease to be; if he is new, he never was. Novelty testifies to a beginning; antiquity threatens an end. But God is as far removed from beginning and end as he is from time itself—the arbiter and measurer of both.
